source_refs.note: Topic printed as 7.10, printed pages 197-198: tropic movements and the four tropisms.

blocks.text: Organisms react to external and internal stimuli. Animals may move from place to place in response, but plants are fixed, so they can only alter their pattern of growth.

blocks.title: Tropic movements
blocks.text: The growth movements of plants triggered by a stimulus are collectively called tropic movements or tropisms. They occur as a curvature of the whole organ towards or away from a stimulus such as light, touch, chemicals, water and gravity.

items: Phototropism is the movement of a plant part in response to light, caused by the differential growth of a part such as a stem or root. Shoot tips usually show positive phototropism, roots negative phototropism.
Geotropism is movement in response to gravity: roots show positive geotropism and shoots negative geotropism.

Thigmotropism is movement in response to touch, as in climbing vines: when a tendril touches a solid object, growth on the side away from the contact increases and the tendril coils round the support.
Chemotropism is movement in response to chemicals; the hyphae of fungi are chemotropic.

blocks.alt: Four panels: a shoot curving towards a sun with its root curving away; a shoot growing up and a root growing down beside a gravity arrow; a tendril coiling round a grey pole; fungal hyphae growing towards a purple circle marked chemical.
blocks.caption: The four tropisms (original diagram for the topic; the textbook has no figure here).
blocks.long_description: In phototropism the shoot bends towards light and the root away from it. In geotropism the root grows down with gravity and the shoot up against it. In thigmotropism a tendril that touches a support grows faster on the far side and coils round it. In chemotropism growth is directed towards a chemical, as in fungal hyphae. All are growth movements of a whole organ towards or away from a stimulus.

blocks.prompt: A seed is planted upside down in the dark. Predict which way its root and shoot grow, and name the tropism and its sign for each.
blocks.explanation: The root turns and grows downward: positive geotropism. The shoot turns and grows upward: negative geotropism. Light plays no part in the dark, so phototropism is not involved.

items: Plants cannot move about, so they respond to stimuli by growth movements, tropisms: curvature of an organ towards (positive) or away from (negative) the stimulus.
Phototropism (light: shoots positive, roots negative), geotropism (gravity: roots positive, shoots negative), thigmotropism (touch: tendrils coil) and chemotropism (chemicals: fungal hyphae).
